content.value_statement: Brand assets can drift from Anthropic color and typography guidance. This skill helps apply referenced colors, fonts, and visual styling to presentations, documents, and design drafts.
actual_capabilities: Lists Anthropic-style main colors with exact hex values.
Lists orange, blue, and green accent colors for visual elements.
Specifies Poppins for headings and Lora for body text.
Documents Arial and Georgia fallback fonts for broader compatibility.
Describes applying colors through python-pptx RGBColor for presentation work.
Guides visual restyling of artifacts that need Anthropic-style formatting.
limitations: It does not include scripts or assets that automatically edit files.
Poppins and Lora must be installed for the closest typography match.
The community guidance should be checked against current official brand rules.
It does not provide legal approval for trademark or brand use.

use_cases.title: Restyle Presentation Slides
use_cases.description: Apply the listed colors, fonts, and accent treatment to an existing slide deck while preserving its message.

use_cases.title: Format Technical Documents
use_cases.description: Bring reports, handouts, and internal docs closer to the documented visual style.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Use the color and typography guidance to align launch visuals, one-pagers, and draft social assets.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Styling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brand-guidelines-community skill to restyle this artifact with the listed colors and typography. Preserve the content and summarize the visual changes.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh a Slide Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this skill to my presentation. Use Poppins for headings, Lora for body text, and the accent colors for shapes. Keep every slide readable.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Brand Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this artifact against the skill's colors, typography, and shape guidance. List mismatches and give prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Define Reusable Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill as the visual baseline, define reusable styles for headings, body text, backgrounds, accents, and slide elements. Include accessibility notes.

output_examples.input: A product update presentation with mixed fonts and inconsistent colors.
output_examples.output: The deck uses Poppins-style headings, Lora-style body text, dark and light backgrounds, and orange, blue, and green accents for shapes.

output_examples.input: A one-page technical handout that needs a cleaner brand-aligned visual style.
output_examples.output: The handout receives a restrained color palette, clearer heading hierarchy, readable body typography, and subtle accent elements.

best_practices: Verify the latest official brand rules before publishing external materials.
Use the accent colors sparingly so the main content stays readable.
Check contrast and font availability after applying the style guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not treat this community skill as official legal brand approval.
Do not replace content structure with decorative styling alone.
Do not rely on custom fonts without testing fallback rendering.

faq.question: Does this skill include official Anthropic assets?
faq.answer: No. It provides documented color and typography guidance, but it does not bundle official image assets.

faq.question: Can it edit PowerPoint files directly?
faq.answer: The skill describes color application for python-pptx workflows, but it does not include an editing script.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are custom fonts required?
faq.answer: No. The skill names Arial and Georgia as fallbacks when Poppins and Lora are unavailable.

faq.question: Is this suitable for external marketing work?
faq.answer: It can help draft visual styling, but published materials should be reviewed against official brand rules.

faq.question: Does the skill run shell commands?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The flagged backticks are Markdown formatting around color values.
